BREAKING: The 15 largest S&P 500 stocks now account for a record 46.7% of the index’s market value.

By comparison, during the 2000 Dot-Com Bubble, the 15 largest stocks accounted for 27.2% of the S&P 500.

The remaining 485 stocks represent just 53.3%  of the S&P 500’s market cap.

This comes as Nvidia, $NVDA, Apple, $AAPL, Alphabet, $GOOGL, and Microsoft, $MSFT, account for 7.5%, 7.1%, 5.9%, and 5.6%, respectively, or 26.1% combined.

This means just 4 stocks account for more than the next 11 combined.

Furthermore, the combined market cap of the 5 largest stocks now equals that of the bottom 434 stocks in the index, the largest gap on record.

Market concentration is at historic extremes.

posts.name: WOLF
posts.text:
BILL GATES ONCE SAID TECH STOCKS SHOULD TRADE AT LOWER MULTIPLES THAN COCA-COLA 

He said it in 1998, sitting right next to Warren Buffett

Buffett explained why he avoided tech. He looks for businesses he can picture 10 or 20 years out, and he didn't think the internet would change how people chew gum or whether they keep choosing Coke $KO 

"As a member of society I applaud what he's doing, and as an investor I keep a wary eye on it."

Gates agreed with him. "I think the multiples of technology stocks should be quite a bit lower than the multiples of stocks like Coke and Gillette, because we are subject to complete change in the rules."

He said that if Microsoft $MSFT was still a leader 10 years later, it would have had to survive at least 3 crises along the way.

Two years after this conversation, the dot-com bubble burst.

posts.text:
Income ETF Cheat Sheet 

5 terms every income investor should know:

1. Distribution Rate: The latest payment, scaled up to a yearly number. Not what you'll actually earn.

2. Total Return: Price change plus payments received. The real performance number.

3. NAV: What one share of the fund is actually worth.

4. Ex-Date: The cutoff day. Own the shares before this day to get paid.

5. Expense Ratio: The yearly fee. 0.68% means $6.80 per $1,000 invested.

Save this one 📌

posts.text:
The global debt crisis has never been worse.

Japan now has a gross government Debt-to-GDP ratio of 204.4%, the highest among any major world economy.

Italy follows at 138.4%, while the United States stands at 125.8%, which is only below the ~132.0% record set during the 2020 pandemic.

At the same time, France’s gross government Debt-to-GDP ratio is 118.4%, while Canada’s, China’s, and the UK’s are 110.7%, 106.9%, and 103.6%, respectively.

By comparison, Germany is the only major economy below 100.0%, at 64.6%.

The current average among advanced economies is 108.2%.

The world economy is drowning in debt.

ELON MUSK SAYS GROK BOT IS THE FASTEST-GROWING PRODUCT HE'S EVER SEEN

"We're seeing the fastest growth of a product that I've ever seen in my life. I've never seen anything grow this fast."

He added that people are using it more over time. "The usage of Grok Bot per user actually has been growing over time. They are using it more per week, not less."

Musk said an enterprise version will be in wide deployment in a few weeks, and that he expects Grok Bot to use most of SpaceX's AI compute.

Grok Bot is SpaceX's $SPCX always-on AI agent, and it launched last quarter. SpaceX's compute capacity reached 1.7 gigawatts in Q3, nearly triple what it had a year ago.

ELON MUSK JUST SAID SPACEX COULD EXIT 2027 WITH ANNUAL RECURRING REVENUE OF $500 BILLION TO $1 TRILLION

For context, SpaceX $SPCX brought in $14.58 billion in revenue last quarter, which works out to a run rate of roughly $58 billion a year.

Reaching $500 billion would mean growing that run rate about 9x in a little over a year. $1 trillion would be about 17x.

The fastest-growing piece is the AI business. It grew 830% from a year ago to $7.56 billion last quarter and is now bigger than Starlink and the rocket business combined.

SpaceX is currently valued at about $2 trillion

The US affordability crisis is worsening:

Food prices have surged +34.5% since December 2019, now at their highest level on record.

Rent and grocery prices have risen +33.3% and +30.0%, respectively.

Furthermore, motor vehicle maintenance and repair prices have soared +55.2% over the same period.

Meanwhile, prices for services excluding rent, including medical care, transportation, education, communication, and recreation, have increased +29.2% since December 2019.

As a result, the Consumer Price Index (CPI) has risen +30.4%.

Basic necessities are becoming increasingly unaffordable in the US.
